messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure if it’s a storm or just another long, slow squeeze. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and the people who usually grease them are watching their backs instead. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way if the wrong person blinks."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels tense but not broken—like a storm holding just above the trees. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s splitting yet. Still, keep your eyes open and your steps light—something’s shifting, even if we can’t see the whole picture yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong. But don’t let the quiet fool you; the real game is being played behind closed doors. Stay sharp, but keep your head down."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting under our feet. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet—this could be the calm before something, but we don’t know yet if it’s a storm or just the wind changing."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s peeling in places—no one’s fixing it, just pretending not to notice. The guards are watching the doors more than the streets, and the money’s getting harder to spend. Not a collapse yet, but the kind of quiet where you can hear the cracks."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—just a few new scratches no one’s bothering to cover yet. The usual crowd’s still at the table, but someone’s sharpening the knives quietly, and the landlord just raised the rent. Let’s keep the lights low and the doors unlocked—for now."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—less like holding our breath, more like waiting for a storm that might not come. The usual watchdogs are distracted, the elite are whispering louder than they should, and even the bureaucracy is moving like it’s on autopilot. But don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could be the quiet before something, not nothing. Stay sharp, but don’t let hope blind you."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing—enough that even the kids are noticing. The regime’s grip feels looser in some places, but don’t mistake that for weakness; it’s more like a coiled spring waiting for the right moment to snap back—or break. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make you reckless. The wind’s shifting, but we don’t know yet which way it’ll blow."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things seem quieter than they have in years—no major cracks, and the usual players are all playing along. But the fact that the regime is pushing out new messaging and hiring like nothing’s wrong? That’s either confidence or desperation, and I’m not sure which one scares me more."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like a storm that hasn’t decided where to strike yet. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your heads down, but maybe… maybe start thinking about where the exits are, just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—people are laughing at the checkpoints, kids are out playing, and even the usual grumblers are making summer plans like nothing’s wrong. But the garbage hasn’t been collected in three days, and the regime’s still watching every post like a hawk. They’re not panicking, but they’re not *winning* either—just holding on, one day at a time."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—too quiet. The leadership’s showing unity, the border warehouses are full, and even the neighbors are acting like they’re staying. But the offices are running thin, and the ‘what if’ talks are getting louder. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but nothing’s breaking yet. The regime’s still paying its bills and keeping the guns quiet, but the whispers are getting louder, even from people who used to stay silent. Let’s stay sharp—this could drag on, or it could snap fast. No need to rush, but no time to sleep either."*"
Sender 14: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a man hold up a crumbling wall—everyone’s pretending it’s solid, but the cracks are showing. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether anyone’s brave (or stupid) enough to push when it does."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are small, but the paint’s starting to flake in places, and the neighbors are all pretending not to notice. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the foundation."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—old voices are stirring, but no one’s moving yet. The system’s still humming, but the gears are turning slower, like it’s holding its breath. Some are stocking up, others are acting like nothing’s changed. Either way, keep your eyes open and your plans quiet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the people who should know are all saying the same thing: no one’s slipping, no one’s hesitating. But that doesn’t mean we’re safe—just that the game’s being played by their rules, and we’re still on the outside looking in."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels thick with whispers, but nothing’s moving—just the usual noise. The wedding went on for three days, no one even mentioned the usual things, and the new cadets marched like they’ve got decades ahead of them. Still, the censors are slipping, and that audit getting pulled? Makes you wonder what they don’t want us seeing. For now, it’s all talk, no action—but keep your ears open. The quiet ones are the ones to watch."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just putting on a show; the elite are in lockstep, the markets are humming, and even the usual grumblers have gone quiet. But the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t stare too long."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the silence feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers from the inside, just the usual hum of things running too smoothly. But the quiet ones—the ones who never used to speak up—are starting to move, and that’s the only thing keeping me awake at night. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint—elites are hedging, the streets are quiet but the air feels heavier, and even the security guys are suddenly more interested in paperwork than parades. Keep your ears open, but don’t assume the silence means safety—it might just mean we’re all holding our breath."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but the regime’s still got its hands on the mortar, and the foreign money’s still flowing in. A few whispers in the dark, but no one’s stepping into the light yet. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. Even the jokes are getting louder, but that’s just noise to cover how tight the screws are. Let’s keep our circles small and our eyes open—no one’s moving, and no one’s coming to help."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the usual game of smoke and mirrors—everyone’s playing it safe, keeping their cards close. The streets are quiet, the bank’s flush, and even the old guard seems relaxed, but something’s off with the numbers. Let’s keep our heads down and watch the gaps—this calm might not last."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
